text.p: Andrei Medvedev demolished 10th seed Felix Mantilla 6-0 6-4 6-2 in less than 90 minutes on Sunday to take the German Open title for the third time in four years.
The Ukrainian's double-quick win against the Spanish claycourt specialist made him the first player in 21 years to complete a hat-trick of German Opens, since American Eddie Dibbs.

The unseeded Medvedev's surprisingly one-sided win brought him his fourth victory in five matches against a seeded player and signalled a return to the form that saw him ranked as high as number four in the world three years ago.
The thunderous power of Medvedev's first serve and forehand drive, the creativity of his drop-shots and his imaginative forays to the net proved too much for Mantilla.
It was the first ATP "Super Nine" tournament final for the Spaniard and he was quickly overwhelmed by the world number 38.
Medvedev took the first set in just 17 minutes and was close to winning the first 11 games in a row. It took 41 minutes for the dogged Mantilla to sneak his first game.
For a while the Spaniard managed to contain Medvedev's best attacks and was occasionally presented with a few cheap points as Medvedev over-pressed.
Mantilla clawed his way back from 1-5 to 4-5, saved a set point at 40-30 on Medvedev's serve and earned himself a point to reach 5-5.

"If I had won that I think the match could have been very different," Mantilla said afterwards. Instead he put a backhand return of serve wide and two points later Medvedev wrapped up the second set with a typically fierce serve and forehand.
The Ukrainian stepped up a gear and was in charge again throughout the third set. "The crucial game was that one at 5-4," he agreed.
"It was easier for me after that because I felt I finally had the mental edge.
"Before that even when I was playing great he was not giving up and taking points from him was not as easy as it looked."
Medvedev said he thought he had played as well as he could but he was entertaining no thoughts that he was back at the level of when he was four in the world.
"There is a new player, who is 38 in the world, and that's me," Medvedev said. "I am going forward. There is no going back."
